answer: The velvet counter is kept in shale and tundra reveals each reset. An hostile operator therefore has to keep each alias continuously active for 29 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. A bond is refunded only after 29 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. Each duplicate costs another 26 dollars in locked collateral and another 11 days of waiting. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
